questions.q: Which childhood gift first sparked Einstein's sense of wonder?
a: A compass from his father
A violin from his mother
A telescope from a family friend
A book of physics from a medical student
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes his father giving him a compass when he was sick at four, which left him amazed and curious about science.

questions.q: How did playing the violin help Einstein work?
a: It helped him process physics problems creatively
It earned him money while he studied physics
It kept him calm before public lectures
It helped him remember equations for exams
questions.why: Lesson 1 says music let his subconscious process ideas creatively, and he often played while thinking through physics problems.

questions.q: What work earned Einstein the Nobel Prize?
a: Explaining the photoelectric effect
Developing the theory of special relativity
Discovering the constant speed of light
Proving the existence of light waves
questions.why: Lesson 2 stresses that the Nobel Prize had nothing to do with relativity; it was awarded for explaining the photoelectric effect.

questions.q: What did Einstein conclude about the nature of light?
a: It travels both as waves and as discrete particles
It travels only as waves, never as particles
It slows down whenever it passes through metal
It carries no energy until it strikes a surface
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that light had to exist as both waves and discrete particles, an idea central to quantum theory.

questions.q: What did his family find by Einstein's deathbed?
a: Twelve pages full of equations
An unfinished letter to a fellow physicist
A notebook of violin compositions
A signed manifesto against nuclear weapons
questions.why: Lesson 3 says that in his final days he signed a manifesto and prepared a speech, and twelve pages of equations were found by his deathbed.
